En-hakkore
en-hak-KOR-ee
proper noun
Hebrew ‘ein-haqqōre’, “the well of him that cried,” or “the fountain of the caller,” from ‘ayin, a spring, with the participle of qārā’, to call or cry, the spring God clave in Lehi for Samson.

📖 Biblical Definition

En-hakkore is the well that the LORD clave open in Lehi to revive Samson when he was ready to die of thirst. Having smitten a thousand Philistines with the jawbone of an ass, the strong man was sore athirst, and he called on the LORD, and said, “Thou hast given this great deliverance into the hand of thy servant: and now shall I die for thirst, and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?” (Judg 15:18). And God answered, and “clave an hollow place that was in the jaw, and there came water thereout; and when he had drunk, his spirit came again, and he revived: wherefore he called the name thereof Enhakkore” (Judg 15:19). The name itself preaches: it is the well of him that cried, a memorial that the LORD heard the cry of His servant in his extremity, and brought water out of the dry bone. Samson, a man of many failings, is yet here a man of prayer, who in his thirst looked not to his own strength but cried to the God who had given him the victory; and the God who never breaks the bruised reed answered him with a fountain. En-hakkore witnesses that the LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon Him, that He openeth springs for His fainting people, and that no man who cries to Him in the day of his thirst shall be put to shame.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The spring God clave in Lehi to revive Samson, “the well of him that cried.”

expand to see more

EN-HAKKORE, a spring in Lehi, signifying “the well of him that cried.”

Samson, sore athirst after slaying the Philistines, cried unto the LORD.

God clave an hollow place in the jaw, and water came thereout.

When Samson had drunk, his spirit came again, and he revived.

It witnesses that the LORD heareth the cry of His servant and openeth springs for the fainting.

📖 Key Scripture

Judg 15:19 — "But God clave an hollow place that was in the jaw, and there came water thereout; and when he had drunk, his spirit came again, and he revived: wherefore he called the name thereof Enhakkore, which is in Lehi unto this day."

Judg 15:18 — "And he was sore athirst, and called on the LORD, and said, Thou hast given this great deliverance into the hand of thy servant: and now shall I die for thirst, and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?"

Psa 145:18 — "The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth."

Isa 41:17 — "When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue faileth for thirst, I the LORD will hear them, I the God of Israel will not forsake them."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses that the LORD heareth the cry of His servant and openeth springs for the fainting.

expand to see more

En-hakkore is the well of a prayer that was heard, named by Samson in Lehi, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name in the book of Judges may know it for a real fountain that God opened to revive His thirsting servant.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the LORD’s provision of living water for His thirsting people in answer to their cry. When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue faileth for thirst, the LORD will hear them, and will not forsake them (Isa 41:17). He who clave the dry bone in Lehi and brought forth a spring is the same who is the fountain of living waters; and whosoever drinketh of the water that He shall give shall never thirst, but it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life (Joh 4:14). The well of him that cried preaches still that no soul which cries to Christ in its thirst shall be sent empty away.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “the well of him that cried,” En-hakkore names the spring God opened for Samson.

expand to see more

En-hakkore — Hebrew ‘ein-haqqōre’, “the well of him that cried.”

‘Ayin is a spring or fountain of water.

It is built upon the participle of qārā’, to call or to cry.

Samson named it after God answered his cry of thirst.

It remained in Lehi unto the day the chronicle was written.

Usage

"Like Samson at En-hakkore, the fainting believer cries to the LORD and is revived with living water."

"The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon Him in the day of their thirst."

"No soul that cries to Christ in its extremity shall be sent empty away."
